title: The Role of Pipe Slope in Drainage Systems
description: Gravity is the primary force moving wastewater through a drainage system, making proper pipe slope essential for long-term performance. If a pipe lacks sufficient fall, liquid drains away while solid waste is left behind, gradually forming severe blockages. Conversely, if a pipe is pitched too steeply, liquid rushes past solid waste too quickly, leaving the solids stranded in the pipe invert. Achieving the correct gradient requires careful alignment during installation and regular monitoring during maintenance. Professional drainage maintenance focuses on verifying that horizontal runs maintain a consistent and reliable pitch from fixture connections to the main sewer line.
